properties.address: 1 W Register St, Edinburgh EH2 2AA, UK

properties.foundation_analysis: Bedrock: Lower Carboniferous sedimentary sandstone (Inverclyde Group / Calciferous Sandstone Measures) overlain by dense glacial till. Primary structural lithics comprise Craigleith and Hailes pale buff-to-grey quartzose sandstone ashlar, bonded with hydraulic lime mortar. Base courses incorporate fine-grained Scottish granite and basalt (whinstone).

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Mature urban broadleaf canopy within St Andrew Square Gardens. Species include *Platanus × acerifolia* (London plane), *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), and *Tilia cordata* (Small-leaved lime). Late-September phenology: dense canopies exhibiting early chlorosis, yellow-brown margin discoloration, and light leaf shed over manicured *Lolium perenne* turf.

properties.architectural_summary: Neoclassical, Georgian New Town, and Victorian commercial civic architecture anchored by the 46-metre fluted Craigleith sandstone Roman Doric Melville Monument. Surrounding blocks range from 4 to 6 storeys with rusticated basements, piano nobile sash fenestration, dentiled cornices, and ashlar parapets. Infill includes mid-to-late 20th-century reinforced concrete frames with planar curtain-wall glazing. Roofs feature multi-pitched Scottish slate, lead flashing, dormers, and standing-seam copper mansards.
